t: A Turkic dynasty, probably of Karluk origin, that ruled from Balasagun and Kashgar from the mid-9th century.
The first Turkic state to adopt Islam, it took Bukhara from the Samanids in 999, bringing Transoxiana under Turkic rule.
Its court culture gave rise to the first works of Turkic Islamic literature; rivalry split it in two around 1042.
dyk: Mahmud al-Kashgari, a prince of the Kara-Khanid dynasty, drew a round map of the world with the Turkic lands at its centre for his dictionary of the Turkic languages.
ev: The fall of the Uyghur Khaganate opens the way for a new Karluk-led khanate
The Samanid amir Ismail ibn Ahmad captures Talas
Satuq Bughra Khan converts to Islam, according to tradition
Chroniclers record the conversion of 200,000 tents of Turks to Islam
Nasr ibn Ali takes Bukhara and ends the Samanid Empire
Mahmud of Ghazni defeats the Kara-Khanids near Balkh
The khanate splits into eastern and western khanates

f.capital: Balasagun and Kashgar; later also Uzgen, Samarqand and Bukhara
f.founder: Uncertain; Satuq Bughra Khan was the first Muslim ruler
